record.title: Xinhua Daily Telegraph reports cancellation of a planned GPT-6.1 Astra after internal evaluation
record.summary: On October 8, 2026, the Digital China Summit website carried a Xinhua Daily Telegraph retrospective whose line 45 says OpenAI cancelled a planned October “GPT-6.1 Astra” in late September after it failed the company’s internal safety and alignment standards. The report provides no named attribution or linked primary source for the cancellation. OpenAI’s current newsroom lists the October 7 GPT-6 Sol/Luna update, and its API catalog documents GPT-6.1 Sol; the inspected first-party materials neither confirm nor refute a distinct planned “GPT-6.1 Astra.” The established fact is that Xinhua Daily Telegraph published this claim; the claimed cancellation and product identity remain unconfirmed.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Xinhua Daily Telegraph reports that in late September OpenAI cancelled a planned October model it calls “GPT-6.1 Astra” after internal testing found it did not meet safety and alignment standards. No named attribution or linked primary source is supplied; the model identity and underlying decision are unconfirmed.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The Digital China Summit website hosts a Xinhua Daily Telegraph retrospective dated 2026-10-08 09:45 whose line 45 makes the cancellation claim. This directly establishes the publication and wording of the report, not the reported decision.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: OpenAI’s news index lists its October 7 GPT-6 Sol/Luna update, and its official API model page documents GPT-6.1 Sol. The inspected first-party pages do not resolve whether “GPT-6.1 Astra” was a distinct planned model; their silence does not disprove the report.

evidence_gaps.description: No first-party evidence resolves whether the article’s “GPT-6.1 Astra” names a distinct planned model or conflates it with another GPT-6 generation.
The single secondary report gives no named source or linked primary evidence for a cancellation decision.

brief.importance_rationale: If the report accurately describes cancellation of a distinct next-generation model after internal safety evaluation, it is notable for frontier release governance and how labs respond to internal safety results. The score reflects the consequence of that event if true, not the truth of the single media report or an unresolved product identity.
limitations: The underlying cancellation claim is a single secondary report without named attribution or linked primary evidence.
The exact model identity remains unresolved; no conclusion follows from the absence of a cancellation notice on current OpenAI pages.
No internal safety-test result or public technical evaluation was available.

technical.claimed_result: Xinhua Daily Telegraph says OpenAI cancelled a planned October GPT-6.1 Astra in late September after internal safety and alignment evaluation. The statement is unattributed in the article and has no linked primary source.
technical.demonstrated_result: An article dated October 8 on the Digital China Summit website, attributed to Xinhua Daily Telegraph, makes the claim. OpenAI’s inspected current newsroom and API catalog provide context about GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra but do not confirm or refute a distinct GPT-6.1 Astra cancellation.
technical.implementation_status: The article says a planned October model was cancelled in late September. No direct OpenAI status announcement, release-history record or dated safety document confirming that decision was found.
technical.mechanism: The report attributes the alleged release decision to a failure of internal safety and alignment testing. It publishes no evaluation methodology, model specification, decision-maker attribution or test results, so no mechanism or safety finding can be independently assessed.
technical.regime: One Chinese-language retrospective article about September 2026 AI developments; a single secondary report, with no named source or linked primary documentation. The article’s product identity cannot currently be reconciled with OpenAI’s public GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra naming.
technical.reproducibility: No evaluation data or reproducible safety assessment is supplied. The report itself can be checked as a publication; the claimed internal decision cannot be reproduced from public evidence.
technical.strongest_baseline: OpenAI’s September GPT-6 Astra launch page and October GPT-6.1 Sol/Luna materials establish public model names and release context. They do not establish that a distinct GPT-6.1 Astra plan existed or was cancelled.

brief.title: Xinhua Daily Telegraph reports cancellation of a planned GPT-6.1 Astra after internal evaluation
brief.why_it_matters: If it accurately describes cancellation of a distinct planned frontier model after internal safety evaluation, the report would be notable evidence about how a leading lab’s internal release gates affect deployment decisions. Its value depends on resolving what model was planned and whether the reported decision occurred. The current record establishes the Chinese-language outlet’s claim, not a cancellation or the reason for any release change.
